chunks: From him, from Fudayla, from Aban, from Muhammad, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'I dislike the sale of ten for eleven, and ten for twelve, and similar types of sales, but I sell to you for such and such through bargaining.' And he said: 'Goods came to me from Egypt, and I disliked selling them in that manner (fixed markup), and it seemed heavy upon me, so I sold them through bargaining.'

key_terms.أَكْرَهُ: I dislike (a legal preference, not prohibition)
key_terms.بَيْعُ عَشَرَةٍ أَحَدَ عَشَرَ: Sale of ten items for eleven (fixed increment)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between fixed markup sales and bargaining (musa'ama) in Shia Islamic jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) distinguishes between *bay' al-gharar* (sales with uncertainty, such as fixed markup on bulk goods) and *musa'ama* (bargaining), preferring the latter to ensure mutual consent and fairness. This narration, found in *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on transparency in commercial transactions, illustrating the Imam’s personal practice of avoiding rigid pricing structures in favor of negotiated agreements to prevent potential injustice.
